OUR APPROACH

Strength.
With something behind it.

Know who you are. Treat people well. Take responsibility. That’s the kind of strength we work on here.

WHAT WE MEAN BY HEALTHY MASCULINITY

A backbone.
And an open mind.

Hold your ground without shutting someone down. Say what you need without making demands. Own a mistake without making excuses. Ask for help when you need it.

You decide what being a man means in your own life. Here, we put respect, honesty, and responsibility into practice. Both people’s needs, choices, and dignity matter.

That starts with being honest about your own part—and recognizing what is outside your control.

FOUR PRINCIPLES. EVERYDAY PRACTICE.

The standards we work by.

01 / SELF-AWARENESS

Know yourself. Check your reaction.

Notice what happens when you feel criticized, dismissed, or disconnected. Learn to name the feeling and choose what you do next.

02 / MUTUAL RESPECT

Give respect. Hold your boundaries.

Your needs matter. So do theirs. Practice consent, clear boundaries, and conversations where disagreement doesn’t erase respect.

03 / EMOTIONAL HONESTY

Say what’s actually going on.

Move beyond “I’m fine.” Find words for disappointment, fear, care, and uncertainty without making someone else responsible for fixing them.

04 / ACCOUNTABILITY

Own it. Then do something about it.

Own your impact, make a meaningful repair, and follow through. Build trust through consistent choices in ordinary moments.

A SMALL SHIFT TO TRY

From defending
to understanding.

“I want to understand what that was like for you.”

In your next disagreement, try listening long enough to summarize the other person’s experience before explaining your own. Ask whether you understood them accurately.

Understanding someone’s experience doesn’t require agreeing with every point. It gives the conversation a place to begin.

Have the backbone to be honest.
And the sense to keep learning.
